subject: Edge POP cascade: maintenance annotation vs third-party outage credit
messages:
From: Kevin Park <kevin@stratuspay.com>
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Cc: noc@stratuspay.com
Date: 2026-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Spike and partial failures at NY-POP on 2026-07-31 — credit eligibility

Hi Dylan,

We saw a sustained period of 8–12s tail latency and a small but measurable error rate for requests routed to the NY edge POP between 21:05 and 21:42 UTC on 2026-07-31. Our production is latency-sensitive and this window caused a downstream degradation for our checkout flows.

We pulled the attached trace bundle (cdn-trace-20260801.zip) and noticed that a subset of connections were routed to a third-party transit provider that reported a carrier-level blip during the same timeframe. Redwood's incident summary flagged a scheduled maintenance annotation for that POP (maintenance-id: mnt-ny-0726) overlapping 21:00–22:00 UTC.

Could you confirm Redwood's view of the incident boundary and whether this would be eligible for an SLA credit? We need the calculation used to determine credit eligibility if you exclude the third-party transit disruption versus if you treat the maintenance annotation as valid.

Appreciate a quick read — our renewal conversation is starting next week and this impacts commercial conversations.

Thanks,
Kevin
Kevin Park
Head of Infrastructure, StratusPay
[Attachment: cdn-trace-20260801.zip (log bundle)]

From: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
To: Kevin Park <kevin@stratuspay.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-01T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike and partial failures at NY-POP on 2026-07-31 — credit eligibility

Kevin — thanks for the detailed bundle. I've looped in Marissa (SRE lead) and Grace (account lead) to help review and confirm. Initial read: there is an active maintenance annotation in our system that covers the time window you cite, but the traces show an external transit carrier error overlapping that window for ~7 minutes.

We need to reconcile two things before we can give a credit determination:
1) Whether the maintenance annotation was a customer-facing scheduled maintenance (we'll validate the owner and the change record).
2) Whether the carrier-level blip is classified as a third-party outage per our SLA exclusions and whether it causally produced the observed error/latency.

Next steps from Redwood: Marissa will pull the POP-level telemetry and our routing logs; Grace will prepare a customer-facing summary and a proposed credit calculation once we have the root cause split. I expect a follow-up with a suggested credit amount within 72 hours.

Quick note: please also send any packet captures you have for 21:05–21:12 UTC if available — that will help the causal analysis.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.com, Kevin Park <kevin@stratuspay.com>
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-03T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Spike and partial failures at NY-POP on 2026-07-31 — credit eligibility

Kevin, Dylan — we finished the telemetry correlation and internal change-log review. Summary below: 

- Maintenance annotation mnt-ny-0726 was created as an internal capacity rebalancing change and was marked as "notification-only" in the change log; it did not include a coordinated traffic-shed or automated reroute. The change window was 21:00–22:00 UTC.
- At 21:07:18 UTC our route-engine logged an unusual path selection that moved ~12% of active sessions to a transit peer (AS64532) that reported a short upstream route flap impacting peering at 21:07–21:14 UTC.
- Error traces (5xx) align tightly with the 21:07–21:14 UTC period; tail latency elevated more broadly 21:05–21:42 UTC likely due to queueing while sessions failed over.

Interpretation options per our SLA model:
A) If the maintenance annotation is treated as a valid maintenance (customer-notified event), the entire time window falls under the maintenance exclusion and is not eligible for credit.
B) If the maintenance annotation lacks the properties of a scheduled customer-impacting maintenance (i.e., it was mis-annotated), we can apportion the window and exclude the 21:07–21:14 UTC minutes attributable to the third-party transit (per our third-party exclusion), then evaluate partial-credit on the remaining minutes where latency exceeded the SLO.

Proposed customer-facing resolution (what we can offer today):
- We will treat mnt-ny-0726 as a non-customer-impacting maintenance (internal label) because it had no coordinated traffic plan.
- We will exclude the AS64532 carrier blip minutes (21:07–21:14 UTC) as a third-party outage per the SLA exclusions.
- We will calculate partial credit for the remaining degraded minutes between 21:05–21:42 UTC after removing the excluded minutes. Using our standard credit formula (per-token availability weighting), this results in a 12.5% monthly credit for the affected service bucket for July.

Attached is a short PDF with the annotated timeline and the raw query extracts (edge-pop-maint-annotation.pdf).

If you accept this approach we'll issue a formal credit memo and the accounting entry against July usage. If you'd like us to treat the maintenance annotation as a valid scheduled maintenance (and therefore deny a credit), reply with that request and any supporting documentation.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior SRE Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: edge-pop-maint-annotation.pdf]

Subject: Re: Spike and partial failures at NY-POP on 2026-07-31 — credit eligibility

Marissa, Dylan — thanks for the thorough analysis and for the clear options. We accept Redwood's proposed resolution to treat mnt-ny-0726 as non-customer-impacting and to exclude the AS64532 blip minutes under the third-party outage exclusion, with the partial credit applied to the remaining degraded minutes.

One ask before you issue the credit memo: please include the final calculation table (minute-level window, excluded minutes, and resulting credit fraction) in the memo so our finance team can reconcile it against July invoices. If you can attach the calculation as a CSV that would be ideal.

We appreciate the pragmatic split here — helps us move the renewal conversation forward.

Best,
Kevin Park
Head of Infrastructure, StratusPay
Asha is on-copy to coordinate finance reconciliation.
